title: Drop static `sh -c` wrappers and cache have() PATH lookups
description:
Two small, mechanical spawn/syscall cleanups. Grouped because each is too small to be its own change.

**Estimate:** a few hours total.

## 1. `sh -c` where the argv is static

Ten production sites spawn a shell:

| File | Notes |
| -- | -- |
| `thegn-core/src/activity.rs` | 3 sites |
| `thegn-core/src/devcontainer_features.rs` |  |
| `thegn-core/src/remote.rs` | likely genuine — remote command text |
| `thegn-host/src/notification_sound.rs` |  |
| `thegn-host/src/integrate.rs` |  |
| `thegn-host/src/cmd/doctor.rs` |  |
| `thegn-host/src/agent.rs` |  |
| `thegn-svc/src/host/mod.rs` |  |

Where the command is a **fixed argv** rather than user-supplied shell text, `Command::new(prog).args(...)` removes a whole process per call and eliminates a quoting-bug surface.

**Triage each one — do not convert blindly.** Sites that genuinely need a shell stay:

* user-supplied templates (`[[tools]]`, `[[agents]]`, `gate_command`, the editor command template)
* anything with a pipeline, redirection, or `&&`
* `remote.rs`, where the text is executed on the far side of an ssh hop

Converting one of those would be a behaviour regression, so the PR should say per-site why it was converted or left.

## 2. Cache `have()`

`thegn_core::util::have` -> `which_path` walks `$PATH` and stats every directory entry on **every call**, uncached. 25 production call sites across 15 files probe: `afplay`, `cargo`, `colima`, `devenv`, `direnv`, `fzf`, `gum`, `ionice`, `nice`, `nix`, `notify-send`, `npm`, `osascript`, `podman`, `sccache`, `systemd-run`.

It does not spawn, so this is cheap — but it is repeated syscalls on hot-ish paths for an answer that effectively never changes within a session.

A `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, Option<String>>>>` memo makes it free.

**Caveat worth thinking about:** a tool installed *during* a session (a `nix develop` entered in a pane, `cargo install`) would not be seen until restart. Today's behaviour picks it up. Decide whether that matters — if it does, cache only the negative-to-positive direction, or add a cheap invalidation. Say which you chose and why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each converted `sh` site documented in the PR with a one-line reason; each retained site likewise.
- [ ] No behaviour change for user-supplied command text, pipelines, or remote execution.
- [ ] `have()` memoized, with the staleness trade-off stated in a comment.
- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; `just lint` green.
- [ ] `test/smoke.sh` green — several of these sites are subprocess seams the coverage gate deliberately excludes, so smoke is the real check.
